channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: YouTube moves the Subscriptions tab off the bottom bar
item.description: YouTube's new app design on Android and iPhone takes the Subscriptions tab out of the bottom bar and puts it in a swipe header at the top. Shorts and the Upload button take its place below.

item.title: WhatsApp stops working on iPhones below iOS 15.5 on 30 November
item.description: From 30 November 2026, WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business need iOS 15.5 or newer. iPhones on iOS 15.0 to 15.4 lose access unless they update, and WhatsApp is sending notifications about it.

item.title: ChatGPT can now make animated GIFs
item.description: ChatGPT can turn a text prompt or an uploaded photo into an animated GIF, then let you change its speed, edit single frames and share it. It comes with OpenAI's new Images 2.6 model.

item.title: Oboe offers a feed of puzzles instead of endless scrolling
item.description: Oboe is an endless feed of interactive games and puzzles, meant to replace mindless scrolling. It was #40 among free Education apps on the US App Store on 4 November.

item.title: Bare is a shopping list that sorts items by store aisle
item.description: Bare is a simple shopping list: type an item and it goes into the right store section, like Produce or Dairy, so the list follows your way through the store. It was #22 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 4 November.

item.title: Inward Photo brings back old photos from your phone, offline
item.description: Inward is a private, offline way to browse the thousands of photos and videos already on your phone, with a shuffled feed and other views; no account or uploads. It was #22 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 4 November.

item.title: Post Club is a little typewriter for writing notes and letters
item.description: Post Club lets you pick a typewriter, feed in paper and type a birthday wish, a thank-you or a hello with clicking keys, then pull the page out to send it. It was #14 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 4 November.

item.title: Daypond: focus timer and breathing beside a koi pond
item.description: Daypond has a 1-60 minute focus timer, breathing sessions and wind-down sessions next to an illustrated koi pond, with seven- and thirty-day charts. It was #23 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 4 November.

item.title: One Cent Start gives you one short reading each morning
item.description: One Cent Start opens each morning to one page: the date, a short reflection you can read in under a minute and a simple meditation, for all 366 days of the year. It was #41 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 4 November.

item.title: Plop Browser lets websites fill the whole iPhone screen
item.description: Plop is a browser that keeps the address bar and buttons hidden until you double-tap or tap with two fingers, so pages fill the screen. It was #49 among paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on 4 November.

item.title: iOS 27.3: Apple will check iCloud public links for harmful content
item.description: From iOS 27.3, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS 27.3, files and photos you share from iCloud with "Anyone with the link" will be checked by Apple for harmful content, a new support document says.

item.title: Siri AI no longer needs a waitlist on iOS 27
item.description: Apple's support page now says turning on Siri AI starts the download right away; a waitlist is used only at times of high demand. Before, everyone joined a waitlist first.

item.title: Hacked websites attacked out-of-date iPhones and Android phones
item.description: Security firm Sekoia found websites in the US, Ukraine, the Czech Republic and Bulgaria that silently attacked visitors' phones with known flaws, with no click needed. It links the campaign to the Russian group APT29.

item.title: CameraStamp shoots through modeled film stocks in real time
item.description: CameraStamp lets you shoot photos through modeled film stocks and old TV tube cameras, each with its own grain and colour, and saves what you see straight to your library. It was #77 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 4 November.

item.title: YouTube's Server Error 400 is back for some Android users
item.description: YouTube said on 1 November that the Server Error 400 on Android was fixed, but Google now confirms some people still can't open the app or load videos. It's working on another fix, with no timeline.

item.title: Google Flow, Google's AI image and video studio, climbs the App Store
item.description: Google Flow lets you create and edit images and videos with Google's AI models on your phone, starting from your camera roll or the live camera. It was #3 in Graphics & Design among free apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: TikTok's chat app Whee is climbing the App Store
item.description: Whee is TikTok's separate app for chatting, sharing stories and keeping in touch with people you know. It works with your existing TikTok account, so your connections carry over. It was #37 in Social Networking among free apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: New app Streamline shows which streaming services you can cancel
item.description: Streamline works out the smallest set of streaming subscriptions that covers the shows you actually watch, and which ones you could cancel without losing a show. It was #26 among paid Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Ellipsus, a writing app for co-authors, enters the App Store charts
item.description: Ellipsus is a creative writing app for writing alone or with others: unlimited documents, drafts and collaborators, comments, chat and version history. It came out on 2 November and was #18 in Productivity among free apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Serato DJ comes to iPhone and iPad with Spotify and Apple Music
item.description: Serato DJ is now an app for iPhone and iPad: mix songs from Apple Music, Spotify, Beatport, SoundCloud and Tidal, and plug into more than 120 hardware setups. It was #62 in Music among free apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Flipcorder turns your day into one retro camcorder tape
item.description: Flipcorder records 20-second clips that land on a dated 30-minute "cassette" for the day, then plays them back as one unedited home movie. It was #6 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Tracery lays a picture over your paper so you can trace it
item.description: Tracery shows a photo on screen over a real sheet of paper, so you can trace it with your own pencil, using the camera or AR. It can turn a photo into a clean outline first. It was #18 among paid Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Local Skies shows the weather like a classic TV forecast
item.description: Local Skies brings the look of old TV weather reports to the iPhone, cycling through the forecast with a ticker at the bottom. It was #13 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: AltoPaint is a pocket oil paint set with no undo
item.description: AltoPaint is a small painting app where twelve pigments mix like real paint, brushes run dry and there's no undo. It was #2 among paid Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Your Stressy turns Apple Watch data into one energy number
item.description: Your Stressy uses what your Apple Watch already measures to show one number, your reserve from 0 to 100%: sleep fills it, stress drains it. It was #27 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Headway's app to find and book therapy climbs the App Store
item.description: Headway lets you find, book and message therapists and psychiatrists, check costs and get telehealth care in one app. It was #39 in Health & Fitness among free apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Pinvoy opens shared map links in the navigation app you use
item.description: When someone sends you a location, Pinvoy opens the exact place in your own navigation app, like Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps or Sygic, or a ride app like Uber. It was #97 among paid Navigation apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Meshy AI turns photos and text into 3D models to print
item.description: Meshy AI makes a textured 3D model, ready for 3D printing, from a photo, a sketch or a text description, without desktop software. It was #95 in Graphics & Design among free apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: iOS 27.3 beta: Siri AI in more apps, new StandBy and Safari tabs
item.description: Apple released the first iOS 27.3 beta to developers; the update comes to everyone in December. Siri AI can take actions in more apps, and StandBy gets new faces on the iPhone 11 and newer.

item.title: Windows 11 update aims to run better on PCs with 8 GB of RAM
item.description: A new Windows 11 update rolling out worldwide is meant to make PCs with 8 GB of memory up to 20% more responsive and up to 40% faster at multitasking, according to Microsoft.

item.title: Snapseed 4.2 adds motion blur, depth blur and LUT import
item.description: Google's free photo editor Snapseed is getting version 4.2 on Android, iPhone and iPad, with a Motion Blur tool, a depth-based Lens Blur and import of presets and LUTs.

item.title: Adobe Premiere mobile adds songs from Universal and Warner Music
item.description: Adobe's free Premiere mobile video editor will let you add up to 60 seconds of songs from Universal Music Group and Warner Music Group to your videos. Adobe says it's coming soon.

item.title: Xiaomi starts rolling out HyperOS 4 with Android 17
item.description: Xiaomi began rolling out the final version of HyperOS 4, based on Android 17, on 3 November, starting with the Xiaomi 17 and 17T series. Phones as old as 2022's Xiaomi 13T are on the list.

item.title: O2 now blocks scam calls with AI for all UK customers
item.description: O2 has moved from flagging suspected scam calls to blocking them before the first ring, for all customers on compatible devices, at no extra cost. It expects to stop more than 3 million calls a week.

item.title: Google will switch off Gemini for students until schools opt in
item.description: Google will turn off Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Search for K-12 student accounts until a school administrator turns each one on. It will share details and timing with schools in the coming months.

item.title: Android can now back up photos to a Windows PC with Quick Share
item.description: Google's November system update adds automatic backup of photos and videos from an Android phone to a Windows PC through Quick Share, without the cloud. It comes with Google Play services 26.43.

item.title: Apple Fitness+ adds Gym Strength plans for weight training
item.description: Apple Fitness+ is testing Gym Strength, which builds four-week strength plans from your goals, schedule and equipment, and adapts each week to the reps and weight you log. It's in beta with iOS 27.3.

item.title: Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo add more than 30 new features
item.description: Expedia Group rolled out over 30 features across its three apps, including Expedia's AI Activity Planner, which finds and books activities, restaurants and events around your trip.

item.title: PocketBuddy: budgets and net worth with an AI that knows your numbers
item.description: PocketBuddy links your bank accounts, cards, loans and brokerages, sorts your spending and tracks net worth, and lets you ask an AI advisor about your real numbers.

item.title: TypeDraw lets you type in your own handwriting
item.description: TypeDraw is a notebook app where you can even type in your own handwriting, with notes kept on your device or synced through your own iCloud. It was #28 among all paid apps on the UK App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Foreweek is a weekly planner for a few goals
item.description: Foreweek asks what would make your week a success: you write a few goals, mark what matters most and tick them off. It was #45 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: NostalgicPod turns your iPhone into a retro music player
item.description: NostalgicPod is a music player in the style of classic players, for your own music library, home media servers, internet radio and podcasts. It was #11 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: Snapshots makes your iPhone an instant camera and photo booth
item.description: In Snapshots, every photo slides out of a little printer and develops in front of you; the Booth takes three poses for a photo strip. It was #37 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: mote draws the weather in dots
item.description: mote shows the sky as a field of dots: clouds, rain and snow in dots, the sun by day and the moon in its real phase at night, and seven days hour by hour. It was #26 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on 3 November.

item.title: ChatGPT lets you lock private chats behind a PIN
item.description: OpenAI is rolling out Locked Chats: a locked conversation moves out of your chat history, pinned chats and search into a separate section that opens only with a four-digit PIN, or Face ID, Touch ID or your phone's unlock.

item.title: Some Galaxy phones report Android Auto and battery trouble on One UI 9
item.description: Since Samsung's Android 17-based One UI 9 update started reaching older Galaxy phones, some owners report Android Auto stuttering or not connecting, and others report batteries draining fast. Google says a fix for the Android Auto problem is rolling out.

item.title: Affinity design app comes to iPad, free for individuals
item.description: Canva released Affinity for iPad, with the same vector, photo editing, illustration and page layout tools as the desktop app, built for touch and Apple Pencil. The core tools are free with a free Canva account.

item.title: T-Mobile Fiber launches a 5 Gig plan with a 10-year price lock
item.description: From 3 November, T-Mobile Fiber offers 5 Gig home internet for 90 dollars a month with AutoPay, plus taxes and fees. The rate is guaranteed for 10 years, and you don't need to be a T-Mobile phone customer.

item.title: Google takes down a botnet of 1.3 million Android TV boxes
item.description: Google led a takedown of a botnet of more than 1.3 million Android devices, mostly TV set-top boxes, in late October. Google says the maker Videostrong built a backdoor into the boxes on purpose and sold access to criminals.

item.title: Perplexity's Comet browser adds extensions on iPhone and iPad
item.description: Comet version 26.42.0 for iPhone and iPad has a built-in store where you can search, install and remove add-ons, taken from Firefox's add-ons catalog, such as Dark Reader and uBlock Origin Lite.
